english.title: Officer / clerk / other employed in Land Registry engage in fraud in connection with search
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being an officer, clerk or person employed in His Majesty's Land Registry

(A)_[committed, or were party or privy to an act of fraud or collusion, namely **(..SPECIFY THE ACT..),]_
(B)_[were wilfully negligent]_

in the making of or otherwise in relation to a certificate under section 10 of the Land Charges Act 1972, namely **(..SPECIFY THE CERTIFICATE..)
english.legislation: Contrary to section 10(5) of the Land Charges Act 1972.
english.pointstoprove:
Date and Location
Being an officer, clerk or person employed in the Land Registry
Commits, or is party to, or privy to an act of fraud or collusion
OR is wilfully negligent in the making of or otherwise
in relation to a certificate under section 10 of the Land Charges Act 1972

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes: Section 10 of the Interpretation Act 1978 states that any reference to the Sovereign reigning at the time of the passing of the Act is to be construed, unless the contrary intention appears, as a reference to the Sovereign for the time being. As such, references to ‘Her Majesty’ and ‘the Queen’ have been replaced in the wording of the offences to state ‘His Majesty’ or ‘the King’, although this may not be the strict wording of the legislation.

other.penalty:
SUMMARY: Three months imprisonment and/or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum
INDICTMENT: Two years imprisonment

Time limit for prosecutions:
None
